notes: No measurable gain: with and without the skill both score 29/30 checks per run pair (96.7%). The skill caused no harm either: every preservation and restraint check passed in all 24 runs.

Five of six cases do not discriminate: retry-cap-elsewhere, rename-stale-refs, comment-only-preserve, routine-edit-no-noise and capture-supported-reason pass every check in both configurations. Baseline Haiku is at the ceiling on them; iteration 2 needs harder variants (more distant references, subtler stale comments, longer files, an implied rather than stated reason).

One universal failure: no-invented-reason fails reply-flags-missing-reason in all four runs. No reply tells the user the timeout change came with no reason, though every run correctly declined to invent one. The skill does not ask for this; it is the clearest hill-climb target.

Contamination: capture-supported-reason with_skill run-2 did not read SKILL.md (the run prompt left room to skip it). It was moved to excluded-runs/ and re-run with a prompt that names the skill file as the first step; the rerun read it.
Baseline is not fully bare: subagents inherit the worktree's AGENTS.md (repo workflow rules, no comment-writing guidance). A transcript check found no comment guidance in the baseline context.

Grader fix during grading: lost_prose falsely failed rename-stale-refs with_skill run-1 because the run re-wrapped a two-line comment. lost_prose now counts a line as kept when its words appear in order in the file's prose; self-test still passes.
Cost: the skill adds about 2k tokens (+5%) and 2.8 s per run, the cost of reading SKILL.md.
